newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares, spooked by Dow, open lower.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares, spooked by Dow, open lower.

text.p: Leading Russian shares opened lower on Monday following Friday's drop on Wall Street, and traders forecast further slippages.
"Everyone followed the Dow Jones," said Alexei Dolgikh, Troika-Dialog senior trader. "The market is moving down."
The Dow Industrials fell 148.36 points, or 2.27 percent, to close at 6,391.69 on Friday following the release of a much higher than forecast rise in U.S. wholesale prices in March.
"I can see Western selling and it is quite aggressive," said Trinfiko senior trader Grigory Pinsky. "It is much more than Russian buyers can swallow."
Traders said the Russian market's steepest fall came in the first hour of trade and were divided over where the market would close.
"There will be no big sales; maybe we will even rise a bit," Dolgikh said. "But I am not especially optimistic."
At 0845 GMT national power utility UES EESR.RTS ordinary shares, the bellwether of the market, had fallen to $0.1999 from $0.2095 at Friday's close. UES preferred shares fell to $0.1431 from $0.1521.
"The time when it will be traded lower than $0.1900 is near and UES will drag down everything else," Pinsky said.
Gazprom GAZP.RTS was the loss leader, falling to $0.590 from $0.625.
"(Gazprom Chairman Rem) Vyakhirev has said too much," Pinsky said.
Vyakhirev accused U.S. oil and gas interests on Wednesday of cooking up plans to restructure the company.
"Since then, we have kept falling, with occassional rebounds," Pinsky said, adding Gazprom could rise in the second half of the day on small orders.
Moscow power utility Mosenergo MSNG.RTS fell to $1.176 from $1.205. "Everyone is expecting a new share issue and this cannot cause growth," Pinsky said.
Shareholders at Mosenergo's annual meeting next week will vote on a proposal to authorise the board to issue up to 800 million new shares.
"We have already seen the biggest part of the fall and may lose another two or so percent," Pinsky said.
The Russian Trading System 23-share index opened from Friday's close of 294.94 from Thursday's 298.24.
